title: Protocol for MicroRNA Transfer into Adult Bone Marrow-derived Hematopoietic Stem Cells to Enable Cell Engineering Combined with Magnetic Targeting
protocol: Prepare phosphate buffered saline (PBS)/ ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) stock solution by mixing 996 mL of 1x PBS with 4 mL of EDTA (0.5 M).
Vigorously mix the PBS/EDTA solution and filtrate using a 0.45 µm filter.
Store the prepared PBS/EDTA at room temperature.
Prepare MACS buffer by mixing 995 mL of 2 mM PBS/EDTA with 5 g of bovine serum albumin (BSA).
Vigorously mix the MACS buffer solution and filtrate using a 0.45 µm filter.
Store the prepared MACS buffer at 4°C.
Prepare collagenase B stock solution by diluting 500 mg of collagenase B in 12.5 mL of PBS.
Mix vigorously and aliquot 350 μL portions, then store at -20°C.
Prepare DNAse I stock solution by diluting 100 mg of DNase I in 10 mL of PBS.
Mix vigorously and aliquot 350 μL portions, then store at -20°C.
Pre-warm the human lymphocyte medium to room temperature.
Thaw enzymes (one aliquot each of collagenase B and DNAse per 20 mL BM).
Mix the bone marrow (BM) collected in syringes gently in a 50 mL conical tube.
Discard any clots present in the mixture.
Transfer 200 µL of undiluted BM into a 1.5 mL tube for flow cytometric analysis.
Store the 1.5 mL tube at 4 °C until use.
Transfer 10 mL of BM into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Add 6 mL of PBS/EDTA (2 mM) to the tube.
Add 20 mL of human lymphocyte medium to the mixture.
Add 175 µL of Collagenase B (40 mg/mL) to the solution.
Add 175 µL of DNAse I (10 mg/mL) to the solution.
Gently mix the entire solution and incubate for 30 min at room temperature on a shaker.
Prime a 50 mL density gradient centrifugation tube by applying 15 mL of human lymphocyte separating medium into a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the primed tube at 1,000 x g for 30 s.
Carefully layer 35 mL of diluted BM on top of the density gradient centrifugation tube filter.
Centrifuge the layered sample at 445 x g for 35 min at room temperature with low acceleration (3) and no brake (1).
Carefully remove the tube from the centrifuge without shaking.
Discard approximately 20 mL of the upper clear solution carefully, avoiding contact with the cloudy layer directly on top of the filter.
Transfer the cloudy layer containing mononuclear cells (MNCs) into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Fill up the new tube with PBS/EDTA to reach a final volume of 50 mL.
Transfer 10 µL of the 50 mL cell suspension into a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 10 µL of 3% acetic acid with methylene blue to the tube.
Gently mix and apply 10 µL into a counting chamber.
Calculate the number of MNCs.
Centrifuge the MNC suspension at 300 x g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Cool down the centrifuge from RT to 4 °C during centrifugation.
Work on ice during magnetic selection of CD133+ SCs using human CD133 antibody-linked superparamagnetic iron dextran particles.
Store solutions until use at 4 °C.
Store MACS permanent magnet, separation columns, and pre-separation filter at 4 °C.
Choose the column size based on the number of MNCs.
For less than 1.2 x 10^8 MNCs, use MS columns; for more than 1.2 x 10^8 MNCs, use LS columns.
To prepare magnetic selection for 1 x 10^8 total cell number, resuspend MNCs in 300 µL MACS buffer at 4 °C.
Add 100 µL FcR blocking reagent at 4 °C to the suspension.
Add 100 µL CD133 antibody-linked superparamagnetic iron dextran particles at 4 °C to the suspension.
Gently mix the cell suspension and incubate for 30 min at 4 °C.
Gently shake the cell suspension during incubation (2–3x).
Add 2 mL of MACS buffer per 1 x 10^8 total MNCs.
Gently mix the cell suspension and centrifuge at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Set up the MACS magnet holder and attach the MACS permanent magnet.
Install the MACS column and apply the pre-separation filter on top.
Equilibrate the first MACS MS/LS column with 0.5 mL of MACS buffer at 4°C.
Equilibrate the pre-separation filter with 0.5 mL of MACS buffer at 4°C for MS columns or 3 mL for LS columns.
Resuspend the obtained pellet in 500 µL of MACS buffer per 1 x 10^8 total cell amount at 4°C.
Apply the cell suspension into the pre-separation filter.
Wash the MACS column and pre-separation filter three times with 0.5 mL of MACS buffer for MS columns or 3 mL for LS columns, each time discarding the supernatant.
Install a second MACS column into the MACS permanent magnet and equilibrate it with 0.5 mL of MACS buffer at 4°C for MS columns or 3 mL for LS columns during the third washing step.
Discard the pre-separation filter after washing.
Elute the cell fraction directly onto the second MACS column by adding 1 mL of MACS buffer at 4°C for MS columns or 5 mL for LS columns onto the first MACS column and removing it from the magnet.
Transfer the first MACS column immediately above the second MACS column.
Push the cell suspension through the MACS column using the supplied plunger.
Wash the MACS column three times with 0.5 mL of MACS buffer at 4°C for MS columns or 3 mL for LS columns, each time discarding the supernatant.
Elute the cell fraction from the column by adding 1 mL (MS) or 5 mL (LS) MACS buffer at 4°C onto the second MACS column and removing the MACS column from the magnet.
Transfer the second MACS column above a 1.5 mL tube (MS) or 15 mL conical tube (LS).
Push the cell suspension through the MACS column using the supplied plunger.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully and resuspend the obtained pellet in 100 µL of MACS buffer at 4°C.
Transfer 6 µL of the cell suspension into a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 6 µL trypan blue solution (0.4%) to the cell suspension.
Gently mix the solution.
Apply 10 µL of the mixed solution into a counting chamber for analysis.
Calculate the number of CD133+ cells based on the analysis in the counting chamber.
Store the CD133+ cells on ice until seeding.
Prepare two samples (each 10 µL) of BM aliquots and one sample of freshly isolated CD133+ SCs (minimum, 1 x 10^4 cells) for flow cytometric analysis.
Transfer the cells into a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 10 µL of FcR blocking reagent to the cell suspension.
Fill up with MACS buffer at 4°C to a volume of 33 µL.
Add anti-CD34-FITC antibody onto the inner side of the tube.
Add anti-CD133/2-PE antibody onto the inner side of the tube.
Add isotype control mouse IgG 2b-PE onto the inner side of the tube.
Add anti-CD45-APC-H7 antibody onto the inner side of the tube.
Add 7-aminoactinomycin (AAD) onto the inner side of the tube.
Shake down the antibodies side of the tube.
Gently mix the solution (final volume 50 µL).
Incubate for 10 min at 4 °C.
Add 1 mL of 1x red blood cell lysis buffer to the suspension.
Gently mix the suspension.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge the suspension at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the obtained pellet in 100 µL PBS (4 °C).
Store on ice until flow cytometric analysis.
Aliquot 100x recombinant human cytokine supplement in 100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Thaw one 100x aliquot before the medium preparation.
Prepare the CD133+ SC culture medium, serum-free hematopoietic cell expansion medium supplemented with recombinant human cytokine supplement (final 1x) and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Seed 5 x 10^4 freshly isolated CD133+ SCs for transfection in a 24-well plate with 500 µL culture medium.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C, 5% CO2 and 20% O2.
Prepare the PEI following standard protocols and note the PEI stock concentration.
Prepare the MNPs following standard protocols and note the MNP stock concentration.
Dilute D-(+)-glucose in nuclease-free water to make a 5% glucose solution.
Gently mix the 5% glucose solution, aliquot the stock (1.5 mL), and store at 4°C.
Use 20 pmol miR per well of a 24-well plate.
Dilute miR in the 5% glucose solution to a final concentration of 0.25 pmol miR/μL.
Calculate the amount of PEI required based on the optimal N/P ratio (here, a ratio of 7.5 was used).
Dilute the calculated volume of PEI in an equal amount of 5% glucose solution.
Add pre-diluted PEI into the pre-diluted miR and vortex for 30 s.
Incubate the miR/PEI complex for 30 min at RT.
Work in a room with dim lighting only.
Sonicate MNPs for 20 min at 35 kHz in a sonicating water bath at RT to ensure particles are in suspension and not aggregating.
Calculate the number of required MNPs based on the MNP stock solution (3 µg iron/mL).
Add sonicated MNPs into miR/PEI complexes and vortex for 30 s.
Incubate miR/PEI/MNP complexes for 30 min at RT.
Label precursor miR with Cyanine 5 dye using a Cyanine 5 dye miR labeling kit following the manufacturer's instructions.
Measure final miR concentration using a spectrophotometer in accordance to pre-setting provided by the manufacturer (nucleic acid, RNA-40).
Aliquot labeled miR (5 µL) and store at -80 °C protected from light.
Label PEI with a bright green fluorescence dye using an appropriate protein labeling kit following the manufacturer's instructions.
Define final PEI concentration using the Ninhydrin assay.
Aliquot labeled PEI in the volume calculated based on Equation 3 and store at 4 °C protected from light.
Label the MNPs with rhodamine dye conjugated to biotin using a ratio of 1:1,000 w/w, dye to MNP.
Mix the rhodamine dye and MNPs concurrently with the preparation of the miRNA/PEI complex formation.
Incubate the solution for 30 min in the dark.
Directly use labeled MNPs.
Keep the entire work space RNAse-free using RNAse decontamination solution during transfection.
Use only RNAse-free consumable material during transfection.
Carry out the following work in a room protected from bright light (dim lighting only).
Add the prepared miRNA/PEI/MNP complex dropwise directly into the appropriate well containing freshly isolated CD133+ SCs in culture medium.
Mix gently by rocking the plate back and forth.
Incubate the cells for 18 h at 37 °C, 5% CO2 and 20% O2.
For miR-specimen: use Cyanine 3 dye labeled precursor miR for uptake evaluation.
Use non-transfected CD133+ SCs for flow cytometry control gates.
Carry out the following work in a room protected from bright light (dim lighting only).
Keep tubes, buffers, and antibodies on ice unless stated otherwise.
Prepare the paraformaldehyde stock solution by diluting 4 g PFA in 100 mL PBS.
Heat the solution to 80 °C and vigorously mix it.
Adjust the pH value of the solution to 7.3.
Aliquot the PFA stock (1.5 mL) and store at -20 °C.
Collect each well in a separate 1.5 mL tube 18 h after transfection.
Wash each well once with 500 µL of PBS and transfer the cell suspension to the same tube.
Centrifuge the mixture at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the obtained pellet in 100 µL of 4 °C MACS buffer.
Add 0.5 µL of an amine reactive dye to distinguish between live and dead cells, gently mix the suspension.
Incubate the mixture for 10 min at 4 °C.
Add 1 mL PBS (4 °C) and centrifuge at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the obtained pellet in 100 µL PBS.
Add 33 µL PFA (4%) to the suspension.
Store the mixture on ice or at 4 °C until flow cytometric analysis.
Arrange the gating strategy according to the representative depiction.
Run the samples on the flow cytometer according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Prepare the complexes and transfect the cells as described in Section 2 and Section 3.
Collect each well in a separate 1.5 mL tube 18 hours after transfection.
Wash each well once with 500 μL of PBS, transferring the wash to the respective tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS.
Gently mix the suspension and centrifuge at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the obtained pellet in 100 μL of PBS.
Add 33 µL PFA (4%) to the cell suspension for 20 min.
Transfer the cell suspension into a new 24-culture plate containing sterile glass coverslips and centrifuge at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and add 500 μL of PBS to the plate.
Gently shake the plate and discard the PBS.
Place the prepared coverslips on microscopic slides using aqueous mounting medium to preserve fluorescence.
Dry the slides at room temperature for at least 1 hour.
Acquire images using a 100X oil immersion objective with SIM settings: 405, 488, 561, and 633 nm laser lines for excitation.
